title: Exponential Equations and Functions
subtitle: Model repeated multiplication, interpret growth and decay, convert time units, and solve exponential equations.

materi.judul: The structure of an exponential function

items.title: Initial value \(a\)
items.content: Because \(b^0=1\), \(f(0)=a\). The initial value is the y-intercept.

items.title: Growth factor \(b\)
items.content: The output is multiplied by \(b\) whenever \(x\) increases by 1.

items.title: Growth
items.content: If \(b>1\), the function represents exponential growth.

items.title: Decay
items.content: If \(0<b<1\), the function represents exponential decay.

isi.content: Exponential change uses repeated multiplication. Linear change adds the same amount over equal intervals.

rows: The new amount is 290% of the old amount.

isi.content: A 190% increase does not use a factor of 1.90. The original 100% plus the 190% increase gives 290%, so the multiplier is 2.90.

isi.title: Example: repeated bounce
isi.content: If a ball reaches 85% of its previous maximum height after each bounce and starts at 22 feet, then \(h(n)=22(0.85)^n\). Since \(0.85<1\), the heights decay.
For an exponential model, the y-intercept is found by evaluating the function at 0. It represents the initial amount when the input measures time or another starting variable.

isi.title: Example: initial coupons
isi.content: For \(P(t)=8000(0.65)^t\), \(P(0)=8000\). The y-intercept is \((0,8000)\), meaning the initial number of coupons was 8,000.

isi.title: Example: initial population
isi.content: For \(N(t)=2000(1.05)^t\), the population at \(t=0\) is 2,000. The factor 1.05 describes the yearly change, not the initial population.
If an exponential model uses years but the question asks for months, convert the input in the exponent. Do not divide the base by 12.

isi.title: Example: years to months
isi.content: If \(p(t)=90{,}000(1.06)^t\), where \(t\) is years, then after \(m\) months the model is \(p(m)=90{,}000(1.06)^{m/12}\).
The exponent must count the number of growth periods. If growth occurs every 2 days and \(x\) is measured in days, the exponent is \(x/2\).

items.title: Population
items.content: Use a factor greater than 1 for repeated percentage growth.

items.title: Depreciation
items.content: Use a factor between 0 and 1 when a value loses a fixed percentage.

items.title: Bacteria
items.content: Doubling every period gives a factor of 2.

items.title: Views or comments
items.content: The exponent counts the number of equal time intervals, not necessarily the number of clock units.

isi.title: Example: squirrel population
isi.content: If a population is 150% more each year, the factor is 2.5. If there are 180 squirrels at the end of the first year and \(t=1\) represents that time, the initial value is \(180\div2.5=72\), so \(n(t)=72(2.5)^t\).

isi.title: Example: doubling bacteria
isi.content: If there are 44,000 bacteria initially and the population doubles each day, then \(y=44{,}000(2)^t\).
Inside the input, the sign works opposite to the direction: \(f(x+2)\) shifts left 2, while \(f(x-2)\) shifts right 2.
When both sides can be expressed with the same base, set the exponents equal. Otherwise, use logarithms or a graphing calculator such as Desmos.

isi.title: Example: matching bases
isi.content: Solve \(2^{x+1}=32\). Since \(32=2^5\), set exponents equal: \(x+1=5\), so \(x=4\).

isi.title: Example: rewriting a rate
isi.content: For \(f(x)=(1.84)^{x/4}\), rewrite as \(f(x)=\left(1.84^{1/4}\right)^x\). Since \(1.84^{1/4}\approx1.16\), the corresponding rate is approximately a 16% increase per unit of \(x\).

items: Check that both sides are positive before applying logarithms.
Use Desmos to verify a numerical solution or compare exponential graphs.
Convert the percentage or repeated change into a multiplier.
Determine the length of one growth period.
Write the exponent using the requested time unit.
Check whether the factor represents growth or decay.
Interpret the y-intercept and function values in context.
Use Desmos or logarithms when the bases cannot be matched.

isi.content: Always ask what one unit of the exponent means. A correct factor with the wrong exponent unit produces an incorrect model.

latihan.question: At the time an article was first featured on a news website, there were 40 comments. At the end of each hour, the number of comments increased by 190% of the previous amount. Which equation models the estimated number of comments \(C\), \(t\) hours later?
discussion: A 190% increase means the new amount is 100%+190%=290% of the previous amount.
With initial value 40, the model is \(C=40(2.9)^t\), choice D.

latihan.question: A ball is dropped from an initial height of 22 feet. After each bounce, its maximum height is 85% of the previous maximum height. Which equation defines \(h(n)\)?
discussion: The initial height is 22, so the coefficient is 22.
Each bounce keeps 85% of the previous height, giving a factor of 0.85.

latihan.question: An exponential function satisfies \(f(1)=128\) and has the form \(f(x)=a(1.6)^x\). Which equation defines \(f\)?
The function is \(f(x)=(-8)(2)^x\). What is its y-intercept?
A squirrel population was 150% more each year than the previous year. At the end of 2016 there were 180 squirrels. Which equation models \(n\), the population \(t\) years after the end of 2015?
discussion: A 150% increase gives a multiplier of \(1+1.50=2.5\).
At \(t=1\), the population is 180, so the initial value is \(180\div2.5=72\).

latihan.question: Given \(p(t)=90{,}000(1.06)^t\), where \(t\) is years after a census, which function models the population \(m\) months after the census?
discussion: One year equals 12 months, so the number of years is \(t=\dfrac{m}{12}\).
Substitute this into the exponent without changing the base.
The correct model is \(r(m)=90{,}000(1.06)^{m/12}\), choice D.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=206(1.034)^x\), what is the best interpretation of \(f(5)\approx243\) in a model where \(x=0\) represents 1957?
options: The account is approximately USD 5 greater in 1962 than in 1957.
The account is approximately USD 243 in 1962.
The account is approximately 5 times greater in 1962 than in 1957.
The account increases by an unspecified amount every year.
discussion: The input \(x=5\) represents five years after 1957, which is 1962.
The output \(f(5)\approx243\) is the modeled account value in that year.

latihan.question: On April 1, there were 233 views of an advertisement. Every 2 days, views increased by 70%. Which equation predicts the views \(x\) days after April 1?
discussion: A 70% increase gives a multiplier of 1.70.
Because the increase occurs every 2 days, the number of growth periods is \(x/2\).

latihan.question: The number of bacteria doubles every day. There are 44,000 bacteria initially. Which model represents the population after \(t\) days?
discussion: Doubling gives a factor of 2 for each day.

latihan.question: For each increase of 1 in \(x\), \(y\) increases by a factor of 4. When \(x=0\), \(y=200\). Which equation represents the relationship?
discussion: The initial value is 200, so the coefficient is 200.
The multiplicative factor is 4, so the base is 4.

latihan.question: Given \(f(t)=8000(0.65)^t\), what is the best interpretation of the y-intercept?
options: The minimum number of coupons was 1,428.
The minimum number of coupons was 8,000.
The initial number of coupons was 1,428.
The initial number of coupons was 8,000.
discussion: Since \(f(0)=8000(0.65)^0=8000\), the initial number of coupons was 8,000.
The correct answer is choice D.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=9(4)^x\) and \(g(x)=f(x+2)\), which equation defines \(g\)?
discussion: The correct answer is choice B.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=(1.84)^{x/4}\), write \(f(x)=\left(1+\dfrac{p}{100}\right)^x\). Which is closest to \(p\)?
discussion: The fourth root of 1.84 is approximately 1.16.

additionalPractice.question: Identify the initial value and the growth factor in \(f(x)=3(1.2)^x\).
discussion: The coefficient is the initial value, so \(f(0)=3\).
The base 1.2 is the multiplicative factor. Because it is greater than 1, the function represents growth.

additionalPractice.question: Does \(g(t)=500(0.8)^t\) represent growth or decay?
discussion: The base is 0.8, which is between 0 and 1.
Therefore, the function represents exponential decay, choice B.

additionalPractice.question: Write an exponential model for an initial population of 2,000 that increases by 5% each year.
A population starts at 8,000 and decreases by 15% annually. Write an exponential model.
discussion: A 15% decrease leaves 85% of the previous amount.

additionalPractice.question: Rewrite \(P(t)=12{,}000(1.04)^t\) in terms of months \(m\), assuming \(t\) is measured in years.
discussion: The number of years represented by \(m\) months is \(m/12\).

additionalPractice.question: A quantity grows by 12% every 4 hours. Write a model in terms of hours \(t\), using \(P_0\) for the initial value.
discussion: A 12% increase gives a factor of 1.12.
There are \(t/4\) four-hour growth periods in \(t\) hours.
